note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: Is fan airflow controlled by a damper or inlet vanes instead of speed?

evidence.text: final element DMP-1 reads "DMP-1 Fan discharge damper" at F-1
no speed control on or next to the fan
Supplied candidate fact, basis unverified: F-1 HP = 15
Supplied candidate fact, basis unverified: F-1 RPM = 1780

data_requests.item: Damper position, control mode and operating period
where: historian or DCS trend for DMP-1 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
site records: existing control narratives, drive settings and operating logs
data_requests.how: Use approved existing records. Identify damper/vanes type, fixed or variable speed, bypass/manual modes and representative dates/hours; retain unknown modes and gaps. A drawn device does not establish how it is used.

data_requests.item: Matched fan curves and system operating points
where: the vendor datasheet: fan pressure/flow and available power/efficiency curves for the installed configuration
site records: system resistance or required airflow/pressure, operating points and process constraints
data_requests.how: Review the document itself against fan identity/size, speed, gas conditions, axes/units and static/total pressure basis. Retain source revision, locator and suitability gaps; a URI or present/readable flag does not establish a usable matching curve.

data_requests.item: Motor nameplate rating and drive basis
where: site records: existing motor nameplate/datasheet and drive/bypass configuration
data_requests.how: Retain original power units, rated speed, asset identity, source and rating basis. Review whether power denotes rated shaft output or electrical input. Do not demand a second unit representation or treat a conversion as measured input.

where: site records: approved existing electrical-input metering and representative fan/process operating records
data_requests.how: Retain period/coverage and coincident airflow, pressure, actual speed/control mode and load timing where available. Distinguish measured electrical input, stated motor output, energy over a period and assumed hours. Record unavailable evidence; this request does not instruct live measurements.

questions.decision_rule: Worth further study when representative records show sustained part-load control and required airflow/pressure can be maintained. A drive quote needs reviewed fan/system curves, operating constraints and electrical-input/load history; the cube-speed relationship alone is not a site estimate.

typical_benefit.wording: Dampers "remain closed so often that they can be found rusted or locked in a restrictive position... the system continually operates against an unnecessary load." Fan "power is related to the cube of fan speed." No % stated.
source_titles: S17: Improving Fan System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry (DOE/GO-102003-1294)

questions.limits: Damper or drive presence does not establish actual control mode. Fan/system conditions and process requirements need qualified review. Similarity relationships are conditional, not a universal drive recommendation or a quantified benefit for this plant.

questions.question: Is electric resistance heat serving a low-temperature load another heat source could carry?

evidence.text: equipment EH-1 reads "EH-1 Electric heater, tank warming"
Supplied candidate fact, basis unverified: EH-1 kW = 20
Supplied candidate fact, basis unverified: EH-1 HP = 26.8
Supplied candidate fact, basis unverified: EH-1 load_temperature_C = 60

where: site records: existing heater nameplate or design/vendor record
data_requests.how: Identify heater/service and confirm the heating method. Retain stated rating in original units, source/locator and whether it denotes electrical input or delivered heat. Generic kW/HP fields remain candidates; ambiguous HP or a unit conversion does not establish rated electrical input.

data_requests.item: Heater operating hours and load history
where: site records: approved existing heater energization, power/energy and production/load records
data_requests.how: State the representative period, coverage and load/stage/cycling basis. Distinguish enabled, energized, full-load-equivalent and calendar hours, and measured versus estimated values. Retain missing periods/gaps; nameplate rating or a bare hours scalar does not establish actual consumption. No live measurement is requested.

where: site records: documented process demand and candidate source conditions/availability
a walkdown: approved observations of candidate sources and distance; no equipment changes
data_requests.how: Review required load temperature/range and demand timing alongside source temperature, available quantity/flow, timing overlap, medium/contamination and distance. Keep unknown availability and compatibility explicit; nearby heat alone does not establish a usable match.

questions.decision_rule: Worth a look when the heater runs long hours and a lower-grade source above the load temperature is close by.

typical_benefit.wording: No source in the reviewed set gives wording or a number for replacing electric heat with recovered heat.

questions.limits: Fires only when the model states a load temperature at or below 150 C, a catalog screening heuristic rather than a validated feasibility cutoff. Without a stated temperature the load remains unknown and this question does not fire. Rated power, actual operation and source compatibility need separate review; no recovered energy or saving is established.
